title: How RB2B prices below competitors' cost of acquisition and runs $9M ARR on near-zero human time
summary: Adam Robinson explains how cheap thought-leadership awareness plus near-zero marginal fulfillment cost let RB2B price below rivals' CAC and unit costs, freezing the product at a simple $79 offer. He also covers skipping VC for lean sub-VC-scale businesses and his plan to build Moltsets, a contact-data brand for Claude Code users, on top of existing content and data assets.

principles.text: Combine near-zero customer acquisition cost with zero marginal fulfillment cost and you can price below competitors' economics.
principles.quote: the incredibly cheap awareness I was getting from my thought leadership, and the fact that we are already a data company with two other product lines, and we have data scientists, and we had this data asset

principles.text: Rivals with higher unit costs and investor pressure can't match a low-price simple product, so they flee upmarket.
principles.quote: their unit economics of fulfilling these contacts were literally higher than my subscription price.

principles.text: Once rivals move upmarket, own the cheap, simple, fast-start slot and freeze the product to stay lean.
principles.quote: If you want to get started in 60 seconds for 79 bucks, we're the only game in town, right? And we have decided to just leave the product frozen in time

principles.text: Design for the leanest operation: freemium PLG SMB funnel, accepting a revenue cap in exchange for AI-amplified low headcount.
principles.quote: it's got to be freemium PLG SMB funnel. And you're kind of accepting a cap on the revenue, but the trade-off is that eventually you should be able to run that with virtually no human input.

principles.text: Sub-VC-scale businesses are attractive: no well-funded competitors chase them, and a portfolio of lean ~$10M ARR products is a great outcome.
principles.quote: If I could just keep creating lean 10 million ARR businesses that are like it's a portfolio of these sub VC scale things.

principles.text: Create product pull before spending money; capital raised too early gets spent on channels before there is pull.
principles.quote: you need to create this pull. You know, and then once you have the pull of product out of you, then you can spend money on channels to speed that up.
